meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator shouldn't be the sole basis for action against a student, and I have it printed in my bag. So what else do you have, Hale, besides a machine's guess?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend, and pasting a draft in from another file is how half his class works.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn the play toward me. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is careless, Hale, not dishonest.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for. And you skipped past what I said about the quotation.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
A timed forty-minute piece in September against an essay he had all weekend to polish proves nothing. Your November 2 notes are the ones I want, Hale, copied to me tonight.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, with nothing on his file, and the rewrite marked before his December 1 deadline.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put that in tonight's email, with your November 2 notes attached.
Do we have an agreement?
We do: a private supervised rewrite Thursday after school, its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, all of it in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still expect that agreement in writing, with your November 2 notes attached and the mark entered before his December 1 deadline. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants all of it in writing tonight, with your November 2 notes attached. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times on the night before it was due, which was dated, tied to his own work and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You opened by calling the checker score conclusive, which let her dismiss your case as a machine's guess before you had shown anything she could check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history came very close to a night like that, with the document created at 11:31 PM and the text arriving in two large edits at 11:52 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the misquoted line careless, answer that point before moving on to the outline, for example by noting that the line appears nowhere in the play, so she does not have to point out that you skipped it.
